title: D.Samuvel Joseph vs J.Mercy Sheefa on 16 April, 2025

paragraphs.text:
BEFORE THE MADURAI BENCH OF MADRAS HIGH COURT

 DATED: 16.04.2025

 CORAM

 THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R.VIJAYAKUMAR

 C.R.P.(PD)(MD)No.1192 of 2025


 D.Samuvel Joseph ...Petitioner/Petitioner

 Vs.

 J.Mercy Sheefa ...Respondent/Respondent

 PRAYER: Civil Revision Petition is filed under Article 227 of Constitution of
 India, to set aside the order passed in Unnumbered I.D.O.P.No. of 2025, on the
 file of Principal District and Sessions Court, Virudhunagar District at
 Srivilliputhur, dated 28.03.2025, and thereby allow the present civil revision
 petition and thereby order to take into file of the Petition and number the
 I.D.O.P. and pass such further orders in accordance with law.


 For Petitioner : Mr.V.Meenakshi Sundaram
 for Mr.S.Kishore Kumar
 *****

 ORDER

The petitioner in unnumbered I.D.O.P.CNR.TNVR01-0001104 of 2025,

 on the file of the Principal District and Sessions Court, Virudhunagar District at

 Srivilliputhur, has filed the present revision petition challenging the rejection of

 I.D.O.P. without being numbered.

2.A perusal of the divorce petition reveals that it has filed under Section

 10(1)(vii)(x) of the Divorce Act, 1869. In other words, the petitioner has sought

 divorce on the ground of non-consummation of marriage and mental cruelty.

 The learned Principal District Judge, has rejected the application on the ground

 that the marriage has been solemnized only on 28.09.2023 and so far, two years

 have not lapsed. Two years embargo has been prescribed under Section 10 only

 when divorce is sought for, on the ground of unsoundness of mind or on the

 ground that the partner is suffering from Venereal disease or there is desertion.

 Two years waiting period has not been prescribed, if the divorce petition has

 been filed on the ground of non-consummation of marriage or on the ground of

 cruelty.

3.In view of the above said facts, the order impugned in the revision

 petition is hereby set aside and the trial Court is directed to number the same, if

 it is otherwise in order.

4.With the above said observations, this Civil Revision Petition stands

 disposed of. No costs.

5.The Registry is directed to return the original impugned order after

 obtaining due signature from the learned Counsel appearing for the revision

 petitioner.

16.04.2025
